days.title: Central Lake and Southwest Branch
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Bellagio
stops.detail: The three branches converge at the center of the lake in front of the Bellagio promontory, one of the most celebrated locations for the beauty of its landscape and for its ancient tourist traditions.

stops.name: Isola Comacina
stops.detail: In the southwest branch, narrow and winding, with steep and wooded slopes, lies Isola Comacina, the only one in the Lario.

stops.name: Argegno
stops.detail: It is the deepest lake in Italy, reaching a maximum depression of 418 meters between the towns of Argegno and Nesso, and fifth in Europe, characterized by cryptodepression depths being over 200 meters below sea level.

days.title: Historical Cities and Eastern Peaks
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Como
stops.detail: Como is a city full of history and in its past it was of strategic importance for the entire region, so much so as to be able to rival Milan.

stops.name: Lecco
stops.detail: On the shores of the eastern branch lies the city of Lecco, which owes its fame to Manzoni's famous novel, which set the literary masterpiece The Betrothed in this territory.

stops.name: Gruppo delle Grigne
stops.detail: The southeast branch, called the Lecco branch, with the city at its apex, looks east to the Grigne Group (2,410 m).
